A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT 'n' p, service_name, count(*) cnt, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'a', service_name, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Several services shift in count and latency, and `reservation` has no abnormal spans at all. Next I'll check the status codes and span kinds, and the per-pod breakdown.

input.query: SELECT 'n' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, attr_status_code, attr_http_response_status_code st, count(*) cnt, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, min(attr_k8s_pod_name) pod1 FROM normal_traces GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'a', service_name, attr_span_kind, attr_status_code, attr_http_response_status_code, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name), min(attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1,3

content.text: Frontend returns 500s (876 server spans) and its client calls error out. Next I'll map the call graph by joining child spans to parent spans, to see which callee those errors come from.

input.query: SELECT p.service_name caller, p.span_name pspan, c.service_name callee, c.span_name cspan, c.attr_span_kind ck, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN c.attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cerr, avg(c.duration)/1e6 c_ms FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces p ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,3

SELECT p.service_name caller, p.span_name pspan, c.service_name callee, c.span_name cspan, c.attr_span_kind ck, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN c.attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cerr, avg(c.duration)/1e6 c_ms FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces p ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,3

input.reflection: Findings: Reservation is the only faulty service. Its deployment shows available=0 for the entire abnormal window (normal=1). Its container restart counter climbed 4->6 in the abnormal window (normal all 0), and no reservation server spans appear in abnormal traces. Frontend's CheckAvailability calls to reservation all error in ~0.015ms (866/866), and HTTP /hotels returns 500 (867). /reservation also 500 (9). Other services have restarts=0. Restarts + deployment unavailable + gap in spans => pod-down class (pod_unavailable/pod_failure, equivalent). Propagation: reservation -> frontend. Other changes (search, profile counts) look like traffic shift from /hotels failing, not separate faults.
